clue.text: Story that has no beginning, that has no end — Jesus, that is a writer!

indicators.note: the story-word loses its opening letter, as if its start were missing

parts.note: a saga is a long story

indicators.note: the word 'that' is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Christ is the title given to Jesus
i.e. (id est) is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: An exasperated exclamation about a story without beginning or end, ending with praise for a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'that' merely links; the second is the word trimmed. AGA (saga headless) + THA + CHRIST + IE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen of Crime was a prolific British author of detective novels.

clue.text: Compiler to slip into a clever and attractive person

indicators.note: the compiler, 'to' and slip pieces go inside the other pair

parts.note: bright means clever
the setter refers to themself as I
to fall is to slip

explanation.surface: The setter slides alongside a smart, good-looking person.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for someone sexually attractive, an informal idiom.

clue.text: Valid core degrees for woodcutter

indicators.note: the core of a word is its centre, losing outer letters

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a degree; two of them

explanation.surface: Genuine central qualifications for a lumberjack.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale, the hero who finds the thieves' cave is a poor woodcutter.

clue.text: Disturbed mind in bigger one that's really big

indicators.note: the shaken letters go inside the bigger-word

parts.note: huger means bigger

indicators.note: a disturbed mind is unsettled, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A troubled mind in someone large, describing a very big thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A humdinger is an outstanding, remarkable thing, a real whopper.

clue.text: Tunnel across in uneven combat

indicators.note: the across-abbreviation sits inside the jumbled letters
an uneven fight; the letters are uneven, i.e. disordered

parts.note: AC is a common crossword abbreviation for across

explanation.surface: A tunnel stretching across a lopsided battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Catacombs are underground passages and burial chambers, a network of tunnels.

clue.text: Read out list of ingredients quietly — lost for time

indicators.note: the quiet letter is lost and the time letter takes its place

parts.note: a recipe lists the ingredients of a dish
P (piano) means quietly in music

explanation.surface: Someone reads out a recipe softly, having run out of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite is to say aloud from memory or text, to declaim.

clue.text: Games of shaven swine?

definitions.meaning: split as S + HAVEN and S + WINE: both haven and wine are PORT, with S in front

explanation.surface: A question about the pastimes of hairless pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a split pun: haven and wine are both port, so S-haven and S-wine each give S + PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Games are athletic activities; and the S-plus-harbour reading gives S + PORT twice over.

clue.text: Vivid in future, possibly

parts.note: future is one example of a grammatical tense

explanation.surface: Something will be vivid in time to come, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense colours or feelings are strong and vivid.

clue.text: It's a safe bet car now got damaged, if held by juvenile

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are held inside the juvenile-word

parts.note: young means juvenile

indicators.note: damaged letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A wager: the car is wrecked if a youngster is driving.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock idiom of reassurance meaning this choice is certain to turn out well.

clue.text: It would be stupid if mother leaves, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: the conditional says the answer would become the stupid-word on mother's departure, so she must sit inside that word

parts.note: idiotic means stupid
mother is MA, a familiar word for her; 'leaves' marks her as the piece that would depart from the answer

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that it would be foolish for mother to go away.
explanation.walkthrough: A subtraction told backwards: take MA out of the answer and IDIOTIC remains, so the answer is IDIOTIC with MA put in.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic language is the natural, colloquial way people speak, characteristic of a manner of speaking.

clue.text: Better picnic

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to better someone is to surpass them
an outing with food, a party out of doors

explanation.surface: Two words placed side by side: a comparison and a summer meal outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer as OUT DO: a 'do' is a party, and a picnic is a do held out of doors.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass is to beat; and an outdoor party or outing can playfully be called an out-do.

clue.text: Some womanising Arab …

indicators.note: some of the following word, i.e. a run of letters within it

explanation.surface: A philandering Arab man, the ellipsis carrying the story into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Oman, the sultanate on the Arabian Peninsula, is an Arab.

clue.text: … still giving pussy a drink

parts.note: a pussy is a cat
tonic is a mixer drink

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, the womaniser stays put while giving his cat a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like an adverb ('yet'), but it is the adjective: motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone catatonic is rigid and unmoving, in a stupor, so utterly still.

clue.text: Willing, after a fashion, when not playing host

indicators.note: the willing-word comes after the other pieces in the answer

parts.note: a way or fashion of doing something
game means willing, up for it

explanation.surface: Someone is sort of willing, but only when they need not be the host.
explanation.definitionFit: A team plays an away fixture at the opponents' ground, so it is not the home side hosting.

clue.text: Serious, lonesome and heartless man

parts.note: sole means single, alone

indicators.note: the word 'man' loses its central letter

explanation.surface: Describing a grave, solitary and unfeeling man.
explanation.definitionFit: Solemn and serious are synonyms: grave, earnest, without levity.

clue.text: Fanatical Philistine has first leaders swapping leaders

indicators.note: the setter means the front letters of the leaders-word to trade places, rearranging it

parts.note: bosses are leaders
the setter Philistine saying 'I have', shortened to I've

explanation.surface: The setter claims that leaders at the front change places, in a fanatical way.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's slip, admitted on fifteensquared: swapping the first two letters of BOSSES gives OBSSES, but the answer needs OBSESS, so treat 'swapping' as a loose rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsessive person is fixated and excessively devoted, like a fanatic.

clue.text: Cow not left in lowland

indicators.note: the not-left word sits inside the lowland-word

parts.note: a fen is low-lying marshy land
the opposite of left is right

explanation.surface: A cow that hasn't departed, standing in the marshy lowland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' is the verb (intimidate), not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to intimidate them, to scare them into submission.

clue.text: Among undesirable persons

indicators.note: the letters sit among those of the following words, running across the word break

explanation.surface: Something lies among people nobody wants around.
explanation.definitionFit: Sufferers from leprosy were historically shunned outcasts, treated as people others avoided.

clue.text: Picaroon's not on? That could be dull

indicators.note: the remaining letters could be rearranged into something else

parts.note: Picaroon is a fellow Guardian setter; 'Picaroon's' supplies the letters with the S

explanation.surface: Asking whether fellow setter Picaroon is off form, which might be boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' tells you to remove ON from PICAROONS, leaving PICAROS, which rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosaic means commonplace and unimaginative, lacking poetry, hence dull.

clue.text: Those leading clubs ruffed Omar Sharif's spade in new game of bridge

indicators.note: the leading letters of each of the following words are taken in turn

explanation.surface: A card-play description: Omar Sharif, the actor famous as a bridge expert, trumps a spade with a club.
explanation.walkthrough: To ruff is to play a trump on another suit's lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossing is a place to get over a river or road, like a bridge.

clue.text: Is priest following god, one from the Middle East?

indicators.note: the priest comes after the god in the answer

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
Eli is the priest in the Old Testament who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: Asking whether a priest who follows a deity comes from the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Israel, a country in the Middle East.

clue.text: Oriental offering obscure problem

parts.note: dim means obscure, faint
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: An Eastern present that poses a puzzling difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Small Chinese dumplings and snacks served together are a Cantonese dish, offered at tea.

clue.text: Keeping away from extremely tempting liaison diabolique

indicators.note: French for devilish: the letters of liaison are wickedly mixed
the outer letters, the extremes, of the word tempting

explanation.surface: Avoiding a seductive, devilish affair, in the manner of a French novel title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diabolique' rearranges LIAISON together with T and G, the ends of 'tempting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolating someone means separating them, keeping them apart from others.

clue.text: As a source of dread leading to ophiophobia

definitions.text: As a source of dread leading to ophiophobia

indicators.note: the letters of dread are the raw material from which something new is made

explanation.surface: Something frightening that causes a fear of snakes.
explanation.walkthrough: Ophiophobia is fear of snakes. The letters of DREAD rearrange to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The adder is Britain's only venomous snake, a likely trigger for a fear of serpents.

clue.text: Nag mouse-like creature

definitions.meaning: a small insect-eating mammal with a pointed snout

explanation.surface: Two senses side by side: someone who scolds, and a small animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A scold is called this; separately it is the small long-snouted mammal resembling a mouse.

clue.text: Store in the middle of the winding road

indicators.note: the central letter of the word 'the' is taken
a winding road twists, so its letters are turned about

explanation.surface: Something kept halfway along a twisting road.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard is a stash or stock put away, and to hoard is to stockpile.

clue.text: Light setback in vote: rift escalating

indicators.note: setback says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A political tale: a ballot causes a widening split, a setback for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' is a verb here, to kindle, not brightness.
explanation.definitionFit: To light something is to ignite it, a verb phrase meaning kindle.

clue.text: Anne McGregor is, perhaps, being alarmist

indicators.note: perhaps signals that these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A woman named Anne McGregor is said to be spreading panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Scaremongering is spreading alarming rumours, behaving as an alarmist does.
